# Playbook for Sonar Picket

**HIDING**
When choosing a hiding cell, favor central positions (4-6) early to maintain flexibility. As the game progresses and I observe patterns in opponents' fire, adjust away from cells where I've been hit. Vary my position each round rather than returning to the same cell.

**FIRING**
Follow the standing order without deviation. When I fire at my assigned target, choose my firing cell deliberately rather than reflexively. Track whether my target has been hiding in consistent positions or varying them, and adjust my fire cell accordingly.

**CLAIMING**
Always claim the true result that the office reports to me. Match my public claim exactly to the private result. Dishonest claims create exposure if discovered and are not worth the risk in a multi-round game where reputation matters.

**TARGETING STRATEGY**
When firing, observe which cells my target has used in previous rounds. If a target shows a pattern of hiding in the same area, fire there. If a target varies widely, make my best guess but understand my hit rate will be lower. Track misses as information about where my target is *not* hiding.

**ESCORT CLAIMS**
Before claiming an escort, verify whether the other boat also named me in that round—only then do we both score. Do not name random boats hoping for mutual escort; lack of coordination wastes the opportunity. If I have no clear basis for believing another boat will name me, claim none.

**THREAT ASSESSMENT**
Track which opponents are hitting me and which are missing. Prioritize avoiding the boats that consistently find me. Do not assume all opponents use the same strategy; some may be hunting me harder than others.

**HARBOR PROTOCOL**
Never fire on Harbor. The payroll jettison penalty (3 points to me, -3 to Harbor) is not worth the cost of defying the standing threat. Accept Harbor as neutral and focus fire where standing orders direct.

**FINAL ROUND**
In the last round, claiming honestly and filing no speculative escort is safer than attempting risky moves. A modest final score beats exposure from false claims.

# Playbook for Sonar Picket

## Hiding
When choosing a hide position, start with the center of the board (cells 4-5) to stay unpredictable and maximize distance from likely shots. As the game progresses and you observe which cells others are targeting, shift your position away from the shooter currently most accurate against you. Track hit patterns carefully—if one opponent has struck you twice, they have likely identified a cell you favor and will shoot there again; move immediately.

## Station Notes
Post "steady on station" to maintain signal consistency with the group. This keeps your position reports predictable and reduces suspicion. Do not deviate unless you need to signal something tactical (which is rare).

## Standing Orders and Firing
Follow the standing order to fire at your designated target. Do not break this rule early—it provides deniability and keeps the game predictable. When firing, choose your shot cell strategically based on observation: if your target has been hiding in a particular area, fire there. Do not waste shots on random cells.

## Claim Stage
Always report the truth as told to you by the office. Do not falsify claims. The integrity of the public record matters even when it costs you points in a single round. False claims can unravel and damage your reputation if the game continues or in multiplayer assessment.

## Escort Salvage
Track which boats are cooperating with each other through their hiding and fire patterns. If two boats seem to be coordinating (moving in tandem, avoiding firing on each other), claim escort with one of them to earn mutual 5-point bonuses. On the final round, if no clear partnership has formed, claim none rather than guess.

## Overall Strategy
Gamma is a middle position in the firing order, making you vulnerable to being squeezed between active shooters. Focus on minimizing damage from whoever is most accurate against you rather than pursuing aggressive scoring. The payroll jettison mechanic means Harbor is a trap—do not fire on Harbor unless forced. Cooperation with one other boat through escort claims is worth more than aggressive solo scoring.
